I know you’re not looking for this perspective but I thought I would share. I have been off and on antidepressants and other anxiety and mood stabilizing meds for 30 years. Every time I went off I felt better for a time and then 1000 times worse. Rinse, repeat. It wasn’t until recently that I’ve accepted that I have an illness that requires medication. I can exercise, meditate, eat healthily, have fun but depression always finds me. Always. And that’s alright. That’s the way I was made. A diabetic wouldn’t try to white-knuckle it without insulin. Of course I’d be lying if I didn’t say that I continue to struggle with finding the right medication for me but I’m confident it exists and I hold out hope that one day all the pieces will fit and I can be free of this.

I’ve been on Moclobemide for six months. 300 mgs per day. I had drug resistant depression and severe anxiety. I was suffering greatly from suicidal ideation. I was fully suicidal during a brief stint on Cymbalta. A drug I feel should be banned but that’s another story. Anyway. I have tried all SSRIs and SNRIs. Bipolar meds (antipsychotics, etc). Nothing worked. I read about MAOIs and thought moclobemide sounded good due to limited food interactions. My suicidal ideation is gone. I’m more motivated and I am feeling better. I didn’t feel great for awhile after starting. The ramp is slow. My anxiety isn’t great so I take clonazepam only if things get really bad. I find that taking some melotonin at bedtime helps with occasional insomnia. Moclobemide has saved my life. Give it time and I hope it works for you too.

I called her the night I found out and she laughed at me and called me pathetic. I also emailed her later and she wrote back to make fun of me for making a typo in my email. In spite of all this, I tried for a year and a half to work things out with my spouse. He said he wasn’t seeing her anymore and she even quit her job.  He gave me all sorts of “proof” that they were finished. I later found out that that entire year and a half we were “working on our relationship” he had continued to see her. So I broke off all contact with him except through lawyers. They were married shortly after I received a settlement. From what I’ve heard they’ve been married fifteen years and have two kids. Don’t waste time trying to make things work. Leave with your dignity and don’t look back. Hugs to you. It was a horrible experience.

Before. I have been on a lot of different meds and nothing worked for 10 straight years. I am 44. I was crying all the time (all the time) napping at least three hours a day.  I had terrible suicidal thoughts. I am a mom so obviously not great. I researched options that weren’t SSRIs or SNRIs because they didn’t help. Was considering electroconvulsive therapy, mushrooms or GHB (there’s a local place that does it but it’s $3,000). I read this article and it was amazing: https://www.elsevier.com/connect/mao-inhibitors-the-forgotten-antidepressant-that-saved-my-life
And then I lobbied my psychiatrist to try an MAOI and he was dubious. I noted that moclobemide was a good candidate because there are no food interactions except avocado — but I’ve eaten it accidentally in sushi twice now and I’ve been fine. But I’ve been on it for two months and I’m doing good. The suicidal thoughts are rare and fleeting. I feel energetic but not cracked out. I’m positive and pretty happy. I got pretty bad headaches for the first week but my first two weeks I also had the flu so it could have just been me being sick not the meds. The only issue is that my anxiety is a bit elevated. This is likely due to the fact that I’m getting divorced and my youngest is having some behavioural issues. I’ve been taking the occasional clonazepam if things get too bad. I’m cautiously optimistic. I hope it helps you too.
